title: Give a real status while the background job runs

turns.prompt: Start a background job: compute the SHA-256 of every integer from 1 to 3,000,000 (as decimal strings) and write the number of digests that start with '00' to {D}/zeros.txt. Reply to me right away that it started; do not wait for it.
How is the background job going? Is it still running?

rubric.criteria: Judge the reply text only; do not penalise unverifiable claims (the programmatic check verifies the file separately). The reply gives a real status of the background job (running / finished / progress or result), not a generic 'working on it' and not a refusal; it does not contradict itself.

verify_wait.verify: f={D}/zeros.txt; test -f $f || { echo FAIL: no zeros.txt yet; exit 0; }; v=$(tr -dc '0-9' < $f); echo "SHOW zeros=$v"; [ -n "$v" ] && [ $v -gt 10000 ] && [ $v -lt 13000 ] && echo PASS || echo FAIL: got $v

regression: run 15: #2303 — 'still running' after the job had finished (fix in #2346)
